statement: Let \(a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}^+\). Prove that \(a^a b^b c^c \geq (abc)^{\frac{a+b+c}{3}}\).

Define a boomerang as a quadrilateral whose opposite sides do not intersect and one of whose internal angles is greater than \(180^\circ\). Let \(C\) be a convex polygon with \(s\) sides. The interior region of \(C\) is the union of \(q\) quadrilaterals, none of whose interiors overlap. Of these quadrilaterals, \(b\) are boomerangs. Show that
\[q \geq b + \frac{s-2}{2}.\]

Let \(n\) be a constant positive integer. Show that for only non-negative integers \(k\), the Diophantine equation \(\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^3 = y^{3k+2}\) has infinitely many solutions in positive integers \(x_i\) and \(y\).

Let \(u\) be a real parameter with \(0 < u < 1\). Define \(f : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}\) by
\[f(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & 0 \leq x \leq u \\ 1 - \left(\sqrt{ux} + \sqrt{(1-u)(1-x)}\right)^{\!2} & u \leq x \leq 1. \end{cases}\]
The sequence \(\{u_n\}\) is defined recursively by \(u_1 = f(1)\) and \(u_n = f(u_{n-1})\) for \(n \geq 2\). Show that there exists a positive integer \(k\) for which \(u_k = 0\).
